speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with systemic hypertension; can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, blurred vision, or nosebleeds recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unusual given the lack of symptoms or risk factors; is there a possibility of excessive salt intake at home, or any recent use of decongestants or NSAIDs? I will now proceed with a directed cardiovascular examination to check for murmurs or signs of renal artery stenosis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The finding of hypertension isolated to the right upper extremity is classic for coarctation; please provide images of the blood pressure cuff placement and any available extremity pulse comparisons to confirm the discrepancy. REQUEST IMAGES: Extremity_Blood_Pressure_and_Pulses.
